authority: NWS Technical Implementation Notices assigning WMO headers to RTMA/URMA analysis grids on NOAAPort. The RTMA/URMA dissemination parm files are not public, but these TINs publish the header allocation directly (as MRMS notices do). Header form: L T2 A1 'A98' with CCCC=KWBR, where T2 encodes the parameter and A1 encodes the domain/resolution.

documents.title: TIN 11-42: RTMA operational, WMO headings for RTMA grids (5km and 2.5km, all domains)
TIN 13-39 AAA: RTMA Q4 changes, adds URMA 2.5km CONUS and 3km Alaska, wind gust/visibility

t2_note: Parameter -> T2 character, read from the header tables in TIN 11-42 / TIN 13-39. Each entry cites the verbatim table row it derives from.

parameter_t2.quote: LU*A98 KWBR    u wind component analysis
LV*A98 KWBR    v wind component analysis
LH*A98 KWBR    RTMA model terrain height

excluded_note: Precipitation (APCP) is deliberately NOT in the compositional table. The TINs print it with a fixed A1 ('LEIA98', 'LEMA98') outside the '*' legend, and do not state a URMA 'LEQA98'. Composing LEQA98 by the URMA *=Q rule would be a guess, so APCP is left unresolved rather than risk a wrong header. Same for cloud amount (LAMA98, 5km CONUS only) and ceiling/specific-humidity/wave-height which the TINs do not list.
domain_a1_note: Domain/resolution -> A1 character, read from the '*' legend text in the TINs. Each entry cites the verbatim legend it derives from. Precipitation (E) uses its own A1 letters per the TIN and is handled as a special case in the builder rather than the generic legend.
rtma_legend: Where * is A for Alaska, C for Puerto Rico, G for Guam, H for Hawaii, I for 2.5km CONUS, M for five km CONUS.
